h: Saints, seabirds and a superhero cameo
p: St Abbs takes its name from St Ebba, a seventh-century Northumbrian princess who founded a monastery on this coast. Fast forward a few centuries and the village has had a very different kind of fame: it was used as New Asgard in Avengers: Endgame, so Marvel fans might recognise the harbour.

If you're coming for the birds, timing is everything. Late spring into early summer is the peak, roughly May to July, when the ledges are packed with guillemots, razorbills, kittiwakes, shags and fulmars. Puffins do turn up, but in small numbers, so treat any sighting as a bonus rather than a promise. By late summer most of the seabirds have headed back out to sea and the cliffs fall much quieter.

The water here is special too. The seas off St Abbs and Eyemouth form a voluntary marine reserve, set up in the 1980s, and the clear water and rich sea life make it a big name in British scuba diving. You'll often see divers kitting up by the harbour.
Allow two to three hours for a decent walk round the headland with time to stop and watch. Sturdy shoes and a windproof are a must.

For the rest of the day, Coldingham Bay is a lovely sandy beach just round the corner, and the Berwickshire Coastal Path links all of these spots if you fancy a longer hike. In Eyemouth itself, the memorial to the 1881 fishing disaster, when a storm claimed 189 local fishermen, is a moving reminder of how hard life on this coast has been, and Gunsgreen House on the harbour has stories of the town's smuggling past.
